findings.text: The opening tells a newcomer what Athena is and why this page exists, in plain words, before any detail. A stranger can say what the project is after one paragraph.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The page lives at Athena's address, but its title and almost all of its body are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets one paragraph about Athena and many screens about firstmate's internals.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; headings "States of a piece of work", "Transitions", "Counters"

findings.text: The header's claims about why Athena matters (one model does the work, a different one checks it, each step's cost is recorded) are never shown on the page. The study shows citations, but not the checking or the costs, so the reader has to take those features on trust.
findings.source: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The next step is easy to find, because the header links straight to it. But the install step assumes the reader already has a checkout and says nothing about prerequisites such as a Rust toolchain or model access, so a newcomer may not get as far as running the command.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The firstmate study is careful for a newcomer: it defines its terms before using them and walks one task from start to finish. It also says plainly what it does not know, for example that it gives no test for "in scope".
findings.source: "Words used first" and "One piece of work, start to finish"; "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: The transition cards are dense and use terms that the opening list of definitions does not cover (endpoint, harness pin, stale wake). A newcomer has to jump to the glossary or will skim past.
findings.source: t8 card: "a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead"

findings.text: The page admits that Athena never ran firstmate and that a first reading missed several paths. This honesty helps trust, but it also weakens the demonstration the page is meant to give of Athena reading a project well.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"
